essay.title: The Local Support of the Powers and Its Uncertain Premise

paragraphs.text: The theme is defined by three member claims, each establishing the support of the powers. Jointly, they establish that the flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself but has an order-less support, the great Lord, and that this support is required by the structure of ordered experience.

The support so established is local: the claims establish the local support of the powers, not every claim about the universal Self. The boundary thus leaves unresolved any broader claims about the universal Self.

The load-bearing point is that the verse establishes the support of the powers by introducing that support; the following argument depends on this introduction. If this premise is removed, the argument has no support.
This load-bearing commitment is underdetermined, since akrama is uncertain. The precise sense of akrama remains uncertain, and this unresolved element is part of the argument's recorded uncertainty.

essay.conclusion: The verse establishes the local support of the powers by introducing that support, and this support is required by ordered experience. Yet because akrama remains uncertain, the load-bearing premise is underdetermined, and broader claims about the universal Self remain outside the boundary.

essay.title: The Flash and Its Order-less Support: A Reading of the kramasadbhava Passage

sections.heading: The Verse and the Support of the Powers

paragraphs.text: The dossier presents the claim that the verse establishes the support of the powers. The function of this claim is to introduce the support, and the following argument depends on it. The three members of the theme all enter with the role of defining this result, so the verse’s introduction of the support is not a marginal observation but the very point from which the subsequent reasoning proceeds.

Because the support is introduced by the verse and the following argument depends on it, the support must be understood as being established within the passage itself. The claim is therefore not an external imposition on the verse, but the conclusion of the given argument: the flashing is not the order itself but is locally supported by the great Lord.

sections.heading: Why the Flashing Is Not the Order Itself

paragraphs.text: The synthesis states that the verse and its surrounding passage jointly establish that the flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself. Rather, the flashing has a support that is order-less (akrama), the great Lord. This is the load-bearing assertion of the argument: it directly identifies the flashing’s relation to an order-less support, and without this assertion the conclusion would have no substantive content.

The argument’s inference runs from the verse’s introduction of the support to the passage’s explicit assertion that the flashing is not the order itself. Since the support is required by the structure of ordered experience, the flashing must be understood as locally supported by the great Lord rather than as being the order itself. The term akrama, however, is marked as uncertain, and this uncertainty must be kept in view.

The passage establishes that the order-less support is required by the structure of ordered experience. This means that ordered experience is not self-sufficient: it rests on a local support that is not itself ordered. The support is the great Lord, and it is this local support that the verse introduces through the claim about the powers.

The boundary of the claim is explicit: it establishes the local support of the powers, not every claim about the universal Self. The conclusion is therefore deliberately delimited. The local support required by ordered experience should not be expanded into an essay-level thesis or a cross-traditional or modern application.

sections.heading: Uncertainty and the Limits of the Reading

paragraphs.text: Because akrama (‘order-less’) is marked as uncertain, it remains unresolved whether the verse actually posits a separate ontological support for the flashing, or whether the apparent support is only a logical fiction introduced by the interpretation rather than something the text itself establishes. The reading presented here therefore cannot claim to have settled the ontological status of the support.

Within these limits, the convergent result is still substantive: the flashing is not the order itself, and its relation to the great Lord is what the verse establishes as the support of the powers. The boundary of the claim, however, keeps this result local. The essay does not extend the conclusion to every claim about the universal Self, nor does it venture beyond the passage into cross-traditional or modern application.

essay.conclusion: The flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself but is locally supported by the order-less great Lord; this support is required for ordered experience, and the claim is delimited to this local support and does not extend to every claim about the universal Self, while the term akrama remains marked as uncertain.
essay.boundary: It establishes the local support, not every claim about the universal Self.

essay.title: The Local Support of the Powers: The Thematic Role of kramasadbhava:v3

paragraphs.text: According to the available evidence, candidate theme 1 is constituted by three member claims — kramasadbhava:v1, kramasadbhava:v3, and kramasadbhava:v4 — each listed as DEFINES. Of these, only kramasadbhava:v3 has its content specified: it establishes that the powers have a support, namely the great Lord, and that the flashing has an order-less support rather than being the order itself. Since the contents of kramasadbhava:v1 and kramasadbhava:v4 are not given, the theme can only be said to be constituted by their membership as DEFINES plus the specified v3 content.

The claim kramasadbhava:v3 functions by introducing the support on which the following argument depends. It establishes that the flashing is not the order itself but has an order-less support, the great Lord, and that this is required by the structure of ordered experience.

The conclusion that the verse establishes the support of the powers is load-bearing on this introduced support: if the introducing premise were removed, the argument would have no support. This function is nevertheless bounded; the claim establishes the local support, not every claim about the universal Self. The term akrama remains uncertain, so the load-bearing commitment is underdetermined.

Because the contents of kramasadbhava:v1 and kramasadbhava:v4 are not provided, how they contribute to the theme beyond being listed as DEFINES remains unspecified. Likewise, given the boundary of kramasadbhava:v3 — that it establishes only the local support, not every claim about the universal Self — the theme's relation to claims about the universal Self remains unresolved. The uncertainty attached to akrama further prevents a complete determination of the theme.

essay.conclusion: In sum, the theme under consideration is presently determined by the specified content of kramasadbhava:v3, which introduces the support of the powers; but because v1 and v4 remain uncharacterized and the local boundary limits the claim, the theme's complete scope is not yet established.

essay.title: The Support of the Powers as a Shared Local Theme

sections.heading: A Theme Defined by Three Verses

paragraphs.text: Candidate theme 1 is established by the verses v1, v3, and v4, each of which plays the same DEFINES role with identical content: the support of the powers. The shared explanation is that the flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself; rather, it has an order-less support, the great Lord, and this support is required by the structure of ordered experience. Because all three verses play the same role with identical content, the theme rests on the repeated establishment of this local support.

The theme is thereby established as a local claim about this support, not as an essay-level thesis, a cross-tradition comparison, or a modern application. Its scope is accordingly bounded to the support that the verses introduce.

The argument for verse 3 concludes that the verse establishes the support of the powers. This conclusion depends on the premise that the verse introduces the support and that the following argument depends on it, together with the premise that the passage establishes the flashing as not the order itself but as having an order-less support, the great Lord, required by the structure of ordered experience.

The load-bearing point is the introduction of the support; if that premise is removed, the argument has no support. The commitment is underdetermined by the uncertain term akrama, and it is bounded to establishing the local support, not every claim about the universal Self.

Because akrama remains uncertain, the precise nature of the order-less support is not fully determined by these claims. The synthesis explicitly records this as unresolved, so the established theme should not be inflated beyond the local claim.

The conclusion thus remains a bounded, verse-level result: it establishes the support of the powers locally, without deciding the full semantics of akrama or extending to every claim about the universal Self.

essay.conclusion: The verses jointly define a single local theme—the support of the powers—anchored by the introduction of that support in verse 3. While the argument is load-bearing, its scope is bounded and its content partly underdetermined by the uncertain term akrama.

essay.title: The Support of the Powers: Pratibhā and the Order-less Great Lord

paragraphs.text: The verse under consideration introduces a specific claim: it establishes the support of the powers. This is not a general metaphysical thesis but a local, verse-level contribution, as the claim boundary indicates. The support in question is identified through the flashing, pratibhā, which is the key term of the passage.

The passage establishes that the flashing is not the order itself. This negative articulation is foundational: it distinguishes the flashing from the ordered sequence of powers, and it prepares the way for the positive identification of a distinct support.

sections.heading: The Order-less Support and the Great Lord

paragraphs.text: The passage further establishes that the flashing has an order-less support, the great Lord. This is the load-bearing premise of the argument: if it fails, the other premises merely describe the flashing’s relation to order and cannot establish the support of the powers. The conclusion depends on this premise most of all.

The term akrama, however, remains uncertain. It may be read as characterizing the support as order-less, or it may be read as a mere description of the flashing’s own order-less nature. If the latter reading is correct, the verse would only describe the flashing and would not establish a distinct support for the powers. This uncertainty must be flagged rather than resolved in the present essay.

sections.heading: Required by the Structure of Ordered Experience

paragraphs.text: The passage establishes that this support is required by the structure of ordered experience. In other words, the very fact that experience is ordered demands a support that is not itself ordered. This is the argumentative function of the verse: it introduces the support as a structural necessity for the ordered powers.

The verse therefore does more than describe the flashing; it introduces the support upon which the following argument depends. The flashing is not the order itself, yet it is not left unsupported: its support is the order-less great Lord, whose presence is inferred from the structure of ordered experience.

sections.heading: Boundary and Scope of the Conclusion

paragraphs.text: The conclusion reached here is deliberately local. It establishes only the local support of the powers, not every claim about the universal Self. The boundary of the claim is respected: the passage’s function is to introduce the support for the powers, and this is what the following argument depends on.

Accordingly, the present essay does not advance a general thesis, nor does it draw cross-traditional or modern applications. Its aim is only to articulate the verse-level claim: the flashing has an order-less support, the great Lord, and this support is required by the structure of ordered experience.

essay.conclusion: The verse establishes the support of the powers: the flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself, but has an order-less support, the great Lord, as required by the structure of ordered experience. The claim remains local, and the term akrama is flagged as uncertain.
essay.boundary: It establishes the local support, not every claim about the universal Self.

essay.title: The Support-Introducing Verse: A Synthesis of kramasadbhava

paragraphs.text: The verse in question serves to introduce the support of the powers, and the following argument depends on this introduction. The member claims of the candidate theme jointly establish that this is the introductory function of the verse. This synthesis presents that shared explanation and its stated boundary.

sections.heading: The Support of the Powers and Ordered Experience

paragraphs.text: According to the shared explanation, the passage establishes that the flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself. The flashing has an order-less support, the great Lord. This support is required by the structure of ordered experience.

The verse establishes the support of the powers, and the subsequent argument depends on that establishment. The load-bearing point is that the verse introduces the support of the powers. If this support-introduction is removed, the argument has no support.

The stated boundary of the claim is that it establishes the local support, not every claim about the universal Self. The commitment to the support-introduction is nevertheless underdetermined by the uncertain term akrama.

essay.conclusion: The verse introduces the support of the powers, and the argument depends on that introduction, although the precise commitment remains underdetermined by the uncertain term akrama.

essay.title: The Support of the Powers: A Boundary-Conscious Reading of kramasadbhava:v1

sections.heading: The Verse as Introduction of the Support

paragraphs.text: The member claims of candidate theme 1 jointly present kramasadbhava:v1 as the verse that introduces the support of the powers. On this reading, the verse's function is to introduce the support, and the following argument depends on that introduction. The argument's conclusion is accordingly that the verse establishes the support of the powers.

The shared explanation specifies what this support is. The flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself; rather, it has an order-less support, the great Lord, and this support is required by the structure of ordered experience. This is the content of the second premise of the argument.

sections.heading: Underdetermined Character of the Order-less Support

paragraphs.text: The load-bearing point is that the verse introduces the support and that the subsequent argument depends on that introduction; if this support-introduction is removed, the argument has no support. Yet this commitment is underdetermined by the uncertain term akrama. The synthesis explicitly lists akrama as unresolved, so the precise sense of the term—and hence the exact character of the order-less support—is not fully determined. We therefore cannot infer from this passage a complete metaphysical profile of the support.

The claim is explicitly bounded: it establishes the local support, not every claim about the universal Self. This boundary appears in the claim, the argument, and the synthesis. Within that boundary, the conclusion remains that the verse establishes the support of the powers; beyond it, no universal-Self doctrine is asserted.

essay.conclusion: Read through candidate theme 1, kramasadbhava:v1 functions as the introduction of the support of the powers, a role on which the subsequent argument depends. The precise nature of that support stays underdetermined because akrama is uncertain, and the conclusion must respect the stated boundary excluding universal-Self claims. Thus, the verse is best understood as securing a local support for ordered experience.

essay.title: The Support of the Flashing: Pratibhā and the Great Lord

paragraphs.text: The verse establishes the support of the powers by identifying the flashing (pratibhā) as something that is not the order itself but has an order-less support, namely the great Lord. This is the claim's function: it introduces the support, and the following argument depends on that introduced support.

Within the argument, the identification of the flashing's support as the great Lord is load-bearing. It is the only premise that supplies a determinate support of the powers; without that identification, the remaining premises provide only necessity and function, not the specific support that the verse is claimed to establish.

The verse also establishes that this support is required by the structure of ordered experience. The flashing is not the order itself but is grounded in something beyond it, and this grounding is not incidental: it is what ordered experience demands.

The theme dossier treats the relevant verses together as defining the same point, namely that the flashing has the great Lord as its support and that this support is required by ordered experience. The present reading remains within that defining scope.

The established point is the local support of the powers, not every claim about the universal Self, and not a broader essay-level thesis, cross-traditional comparison, or modern application. The dossier explicitly keeps those out of the claim.

One term remains uncertain: akrama, rendered here as order-less. If akrama is read differently, the specific conclusion that the support is order-less would not be secured, even though the general claim that the flashing has a support would remain.

essay.conclusion: The verse establishes the support of the powers: the flashing (pratibhā) has the great Lord as its order-less support, and this support is required by the structure of ordered experience. The identification of the support is load-bearing, the scope is limited to the local claim, and the term akrama remains flagged as uncertain.
essay.boundary: It establishes the local support, not every claim about the universal Self.
